permanentSolutions.description: One-time capital investments that create permanent infrastructure.

clean_water_infrastructure.beneficiaries: 2.2 billion people without safely managed drinking water (WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme figure)
clean_water_infrastructure.quote: 2.2 billion people do not have access to safely managed drinking water services. The average cost for World Vision to equip one person with access to clean water is $50.

housing_infrastructure.description: Adequate housing for people in inadequate housing/slums by 2030
housing_infrastructure.beneficiaries: 3 billion people (40% of world population) needing adequate housing by 2030
housing_infrastructure.quote: By 2030, UN-Habitat estimates that 3 billion people, about 40 per cent of the world's population, will need access to adequate housing. This translates into a demand for 96,000 new affordable and accessible housing units every day.
housing_infrastructure.note: No consolidated global cost estimate available; need is massive and ongoing

electricity_universal_access.beneficiaries: 730 million people without electricity access (IEA, 2024 data)
electricity_universal_access.source: IEA - SDG7: Data and Projections (Access to Electricity)
electricity_universal_access.quote: Ensuring universal access to electricity by 2030 will require an investment of USD 50 billion each year on average, including costs for power generation, electricity networks, and decentralised solutions.
electricity_universal_access.note: 730 million figure is IEA's most recent (2024) headcount; earlier drafts of this page used a stale 660 million figure, which is actually IEA's 2030 projection, not a current count.

electricity_expansion.quote: Annual investment in electricity generation in developing countries needs to more than double by 2035—from $280 billion today to $630 billion.

perpetualPrograms.description: Annual recurring costs for humanitarian programs (2025-2026 figures).

tb_programs.beneficiaries: Global tuberculosis prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care
tb_programs.quote: Countries committed to mobilizing at least US$22 billion per year for TB prevention, diagnostic and treatment services by 2027. In 2024, the total funding available in LMICs was US$5.9 billion (27% of that target).

malaria_programs.quote: Global Technical Strategy target: US$9.3 billion by 2025. Actual malaria funding available in 2024 was US$3.9 billion — 42% of that target, leaving a shortfall of roughly US$5.4 billion.

hiv_aids_programs.beneficiaries: Global HIV/AIDS prevention, treatment, and care (low- and middle-income countries)
hiv_aids_programs.quote: US$21.9 billion is needed annually by 2030 for the AIDS response in low- and middle-income countries. At the end of 2025, US$17.6 billion was available — about 20% below target — leaving a funding gap of US$4.3 billion.

food_security_wfp.beneficiaries: 110 million of the most vulnerable people (2026 target)
food_security_wfp.note: WFP itself warns current funding forecasts suggest it may receive only about half of this ($6.5B).
food_security_wfp.quote: In 2026, the agency aims to reach 110 million of the most vulnerable at an estimated cost of $13 billion.

food_security_full.beneficiaries: 828 million people facing hunger globally, including 345 million facing severe hunger
food_security_full.note: Full cost to end hunger worldwide; WFP's realistic 2026 funding target above is far smaller ($13B for 110M people).
food_security_full.quote: WFP needs $40 billion dollars per year to feed all of the world's hungry people and end global hunger by 2030. There are 828 million people on the planet who are hungry — that's 2.5 times more than the entire population of America.

combined_three_diseases.description: TB ($22B) + Malaria ($9.3B) + HIV/AIDS ($21.9B) combined annual cost
combined_three_diseases.source: Compiled from WHO and UNAIDS 2025 reports

perpetualFund.description: The power of investment returns: recurring annual income without touching the principal.

returns_5_percent.description: $1 trillion invested at 5% annual return generates $50 billion per year forever
returns_5_percent.assumption: Conservative 5% annual return on $1 trillion principal (4% is very conservative, 6-7% is typical long-run stock market average). This is a modeling assumption, not a cited statistic.

covers_three_diseases_nearly_exactly.surplus: Covers 94% of all three major disease programs with annual returns alone
covers_three_diseases_nearly_exactly.interpretation: The full $1T principal, left untouched and invested at 5%, generates enough every year to cover 94% of the world's combined TB, malaria and HIV response — forever.

water_plus_perpetual_combo.description: Spend $110B once on universal clean water access; invest the remaining $890B principal at 5%.
water_plus_perpetual_combo.comparison: $44.5B/year covers 84% of the combined TB+Malaria+HIV need ($53.2B/year)
water_plus_perpetual_combo.interpretation: Solve global water access permanently, and still generate enough every year afterward to fund 84% of the world's three biggest disease programs, indefinitely, without ever touching principal again.
water_plus_perpetual_combo.source: Derived from clean_water_infrastructure and combined_three_diseases figures above

sourceNotes.dataYear: 2025-2026 data used where available; 2024 baseline adjusted for most recent figures
sourceNotes.gdpData: IMF World Economic Outlook April 2026 forecasts in nominal USD (see data/imf-gdp.csv and data/countries_gdp_2026.json)
sourceNotes.healthData: WHO 2025 reports (TB, Malaria); UNAIDS Global AIDS Update 2025; WFP 2026 outlook
sourceNotes.infrastructureData: World Bank, IEA and UN-Habitat 2024-2026 estimates
sourceNotes.methodology: All figures extracted from institutional primary sources and re-verified against source pages/reports on 2026-08-26. URLs point to primary/authoritative sources. See SOURCES.md for the full citation list.
sourceNotes.lastAudit: 2026-08-26: Full audit of all quotes and figures against primary sources. Corrected clean water total ($100B→$110B using current 2.2B-person figure), electricity headcount (660M→730M, the 660M figure was actually a 2030 projection mislabeled as current), added missing HIV/AIDS current-funding data, and corrected hunger figure used on-site (783M→828M).
